answer: Each agent’s work enters an escrowed task market: a requester locks funds, and payment is released only when independent evaluators accept a result against a public rubric. To profit from fake identities, an attacker must fund each agent’s stake and produce useful work; identities alone earn nothing, while colluding evaluators risk losing their own stake when audits expose biased approvals. A jade ledger records those outcomes, a falcon flags correlated reviews, and each summit raises the cost of maintaining disposable accounts.
